title: Legalweek New York 2027: A complete attendee travel guide
summary: Plan Legalweek New York 2027 with practical advice on North Javits hotels, airports, budgeting, vendor demos, client meals, and follow-up.
body_markdown:
Legalweek New York 2027 is set to take place March 1–3 2027 at North Javits, 445 11th Avenue. Legalweek brings legal professionals together to examine technology and working practices across law firms and in-house teams, with programming for law firm leaders, in-house counsel, legal operations, technology, innovation, marketing, and knowledge-management teams.\[1\]\[2\]


This guide covers helpful advice around hotels and the North Javits route, airports and rail, budgeting, demonstrations, meetings, client meals, and more, and we'll introduce how Navan Edge can book flights, hotels, and restaurants in one chat.


### Key takeaways


- Legalweek New York expects 10,000-plus attendees at North Javits in 2027.\[1\]
- Compare Hudson Yards, Penn Station, and Midtown West hotels by the actual route to the venue, total price, terms, and loyalty treatment.
- Determine your priority sessions before booking travel, and recheck the schedule before departure.\[3\]
- Navan booking data for 185 local bookings during the equivalent Legalweek period in 2026 found a $397 median nightly rate
- Navan Edge can compare and book flights, hotels, and restaurants in one chat, guided by your preferences and connected loyalty programs.


## What is Legalweek, and who is it for?


Legalweek is for people who build, select, use, and advise on legal technology. 10,000-plus attendees, 400-plus speakers, and more than 100 sessions are expected in 2027. Attendees usually include law firm partners, legal technology and innovation architects, legal operations professionals, in-house counsel, marketers, and knowledge-management leaders.\[1\]\[2\]


They may be working on intake, contract review, matter management, discovery, knowledge retrieval, pricing, or controlled uses of AI. Before deciding if to attend, define what you actually want to gain from it. That could be a comparison of three approaches, an answer to an implementation question, or a recommendation for a pilot.


## What makes Legalweek worth the trip?


Legal technology is hard to judge from a list of features. In person, you can watch a workflow, interrupt with questions, and see what happens when the clean example breaks.


Ask presenters to show a representative task through permissions, handoffs, exceptions, and final output. Then you can compare notes with peers in similar organizations, and record the team, systems, and constraints behind their advice.


If you plan to spend time walk around the exhibit hall, prepare a shortlist in advance and schedule the clients, partners, and practitioners worth meeting. For each important conversation, capture documentation, a follow-up demo, a reference call, or a question that wasn’t answered. This will leave you with a follow-up list that’s realistic enough to follow through with.


## Where to stay during Legalweek New York 2027


North Javits is on Manhattan’s west side near Hudson Yards.\[16\] Staying nearby can make early starts easier and allow for midday resets easier. Penn Station may be better if you’re arriving by Amtrak.

### Legalweek hotel pricing


Navan analyzed 185 active hotel bookings near North Javits and Hudson Yards for check-ins March 6–13, 2026, the prior Legalweek period. The median nightly total was $397 and the average stay 2.3 nights, including taxes and fees.


Note that this sample covers business-travel bookings in the area, but it doesn't identify Legalweek attendees.


## Consider the complete journey, not just the flight


New York has three major airports plus Amtrak and regional rail. Decide the latest time you want to arrive and work backward to plan your arrival journey, taking into consideration any connection risk, airport transfers, luggage collection, hotel route, and of course loyalty preferences. A nonstop arriving Sunday may be worth more than a cheaper connection that lands Monday morning with a risk of delay.

## How to set a budget Legalweek 2027 in New York


Budget for registration, travel, lodging, taxes and fees, airport or rail transfers, local transport, meals, and client or team events. If relevant, also show any optional training.


### Federal per diem for New York City


For March 2027, the federal New York City benchmark is $296 a night for lodging before tax and $92 a day for meals and incidental expenses.\[5\]\[18\] These are federal reimbursement rates; your employer may set different limits.\[15\]


Registration add-ons, hotel fees, both airport transfers and any hosted dinners can change the total. Checking these alongside the headline prices gives you a more realistic estimate.


## How to plan a productive, yet flexible agenda at Legalweek 2027


Monday and Tuesday combine educational tracks with exhibit-hall networking. Wednesday includes focused forums and intensives, with programming scheduled until 3:30 p.m. Attend the sessions most relevant to your role, and leave space for demonstrations, meetings, and meals.\[1\]\[3\]


Monday’s opening keynote starts at 9 a.m., so arriving Sunday may be more comfortable. If you plan to stay through Wednesday’s final sessions, allow enough time afterward to collect your luggage and reach the airport.


Your final day may need more time carved out for checkout and the journey home. Keeping meeting locations and contact details in the calendar can make walking and changes smoother.


## What to pack for Legalweek New York 2027


Business casual should cover most sessions and time on the exhibit floor. A polished layer may be useful for client dinners or formal meetings, while comfortable shoes will help with a full day of walking.


Central Park’s 1991–2020 March climate averages are 49.9°F high and a low of 35.8°F.\[6\] A warm, weather-resistant layer may be useful, but check the weather forecast before you leave.


If you're not staying close to conference and will be out of your room all day, some useful extras could include a spare pair of comfortable shoes to help prevent blisters, a portable battery and cables, a refillable water bottle, a compact umbrella, an indoor layer, hand sanitizer and a protein filled snack if you find yourself needing a pick-me-up.


## Getting from New York airports into Manhattan


If comparing flights and hotel areas, these routes show how each airport connects with Manhattan. The onward journey from the station or drop-off point can help you decide where to stay.


**Airport**


**Public transport into Manhattan**


**What to weigh while choosing a hotel**


JFK


AirTrain to Jamaica, then LIRR to Penn Station or a subway connection into Manhattan.\[7\]\[8\]


The Penn Station rail option may suit hotels around Penn Station or Hudson Yards. Other hotel areas may need another connection.


LaGuardia (LGA)


Free Q70 bus to Jackson Heights–Roosevelt/74th Street for the subway, or Woodside for LIRR service.\[9\]


Public transport involves a bus transfer. The easiest onward route depends on the hotel area you choose.


Newark (EWR)


AirTrain, with a construction shuttle when required, to Newark Airport Rail Station; then NJ Transit or Amtrak to New York Penn Station.\[10\]\[11\]


Penn Station is the Manhattan arrival point for this rail route. The onward journey depends on the hotel’s location.


A taxi or app-based ride is an alternative from all three airports and may be easier with heavy luggage or a group. Once you choose a hotel, its exact location and the travel-day service alerts will help you compare the full journey.


If you arrive before your room is ready, luggage storage may make the wait easier. Navan Edge can also request early check-in on your behalf, subject to hotel availability.


## How to organize a productive agenda that’s not overwhelming


It can be tempting to attend every session and keynote, but there’s value to gain everywhere at Legalweek New York


Product demos:


A demonstration is more useful when it resembles a task your team actually executes. A made-up case can preserve the workflow you want to test without exposing client or confidential information. An incomplete document or missing permission may reveal more than a polished example.


Brief but clear notes separating what you saw from what was promised will make comparisons easier afterward.


Time for networking:


Leaving time for spontaneous introductions can be rewarding. A question from your own work is a useful conversation starter. Hearing about someone’s team, systems and constraints also helps you judge whether their experience applies to yours.


A short follow-up referencing the discussion and anything you promised is easier to continue than a general connection request.


Breathing room:


Leaving time during the day for a proper lunch, coffee or water, some fresh air if possible and organized note taking can make long conference days more manageable.


## What to eat near Legalweek


After a full day at North Javits, a nearby restaurant can leave more time for the conversation. These options suit different kinds of meals; availability, dietary needs and any group-booking terms may influence which works for you.


- **Queensyard for a client or executive dinner:** Its private room seats 14, with other spaces for larger groups.\[12\]
- **Mercado Little Spain for a flexible team meal:** Its restaurants, bars and kiosks suit a quick meal or a longer get-together.\[13\]
- **Wild Ink for a hosted gathering:** It offers semi-private dining and restaurant buyouts.\[14\]


Navan Edge can search current restaurant availability by all these individual needs and atmosphere, and it can book the reservation in the same trip chat as the flights and hotel.\[17\].


## Wrapping up from Legalweek


The final day can feel less rushed when checkout, luggage storage and the airport journey fit around your remaining sessions. A late-checkout may help, and Navan Edge can request it on your behalf. Saving receipts and brief meeting notes while the details are fresh can also make expense processing and the return to work easier.


When you return home, a team debrief can help reflect and separate ideas that are ready to use from questions that need more research. And it can be a good idea to do it sooner rather than later, before you get swept back up in the day-to-day.
